target_moa.text: Evolocumab is a human monoclonal IgG2 directed against PCSK9; it binds PCSK9 and inhibits circulating PCSK9 from binding the LDL receptor, preventing PCSK9-mediated LDLR degradation and increasing the number of LDLRs available to clear LDL, thereby lowering LDL-C.

citations.quote: Evlocumab is a human monoclonal IgG2 directed against human proprotein convertase subtilisin kexin 9 (PCSK9). Evlocumab binds to PCSK9 and inhibits circulating PCSK9 from binding to the low density lipoprotein (LDL) receptor (LDLR), preventing PCSK9-mediated LDLR degradation and permitting LDLR to recycle back to the liver cell surface. By inhibiting the binding of PCSK9 to LDLR, evlocumab increases the number of LDLRs available to clear LDL from the blood, thereby lowering LDL-C levels.
Evlocumab is a human monoclonal immunoglobulin G2 (IgG2) directed against human proprotein convertase subtilisin kexin 9 (PCSK9).

key_safety.text: Most common adverse reactions (>5%, more frequent than placebo): nasopharyngitis, upper respiratory tract infection, influenza, back pain, and injection site reactions. In the 52-week trial: nasopharyngitis 10.5% vs 9.6% placebo, upper respiratory tract infection 9.3% vs 6.3%, influenza 7.5% vs 6.3%, back pain 6.2% vs 5.6%, injection site reactions 5.7% vs 5.0%. Allergic reactions (rash, urticaria) also occurred.
